name: Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics
description: This is an SPH fluid simulation. It attempts to accurately simulate the behaviour of fluid using particle based methods. The speed of the online port is lackluster but I would reccomend checking out the original C++ version which runs very well.
A shoutout to the content creator Sebastian Lague who inspired this project.

The math for the particles works with a hasshing grid that only selects nearby particles, the cellsize of the grid is set to be the smoothing radius, hence why it is contant. The particles calculate forces using a poly-6 kernel, scaled to the smoothing radius.
controls: Click the screen to draw particles in towards your mouse. Change the radius and strength of the pull using the distance scaler and strength parameters.
Changing gravity affects the downwards force, and the mass changes the acceleration due to forces.

Viscocity is the friction withing the fluid, high viscocity will produce a more honey-like substance. The gas constant is the natral force between particles and the rest_density is the target density of the fluid. The damping represents the amount of energy the particles keep in a boundary collision where 1 is all its speed and 0 is none.

timeStep represents the simulated amount of time each frame and stepsPerRender is the number of simulated steps between each render. A higher stepsPerRender can be used to lessen the error that the program accumulates but will slow it down.
